title: Right anodyne maps preserve coherent cocones and give inner anodyne joins
statement:
Use the simplicial sets, quasicategories, functor quasicategories and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Right anodyne means closure of the horn inclusions $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$, $0<i\leq n$, and isomorphisms under pushouts, transfinite compositions and retracts; inner anodyne uses instead $0<i<n$. For simplicial sets $X,Y$, their join $X\star Y$ has $r$-simplices $X_r\amalg Y_r\amalg\coprod_{u+v+1=r}X_u\times Y_v$, with operators induced by restricting the ordered concatenation of the $X$-vertices followed by the $Y$-vertices. Write $X^{\triangleright}=X\star\Delta^0$.

Let $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ be a right anodyne monomorphism. For every monomorphism $k:K\hookrightarrow L$, the pushout-join inclusion
$$ (A\star L)\amalg_{A\star K}(B\star K)\longrightarrow B\star L $$
is inner anodyne. Independently of any existence of colimits, for every quasicategory $\mathcal C$, simplicial map $p:B\to\mathcal C$ and vertex $T\in\mathcal C$, restriction induces an equivalence of Kan complexes
$$ \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal C)}(p,\Delta_BT)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal C)}(p\circ i,\Delta_AT), $$
where $\Delta_BT$ and $\Delta_AT$ denote constant diagrams. This restriction is natural in $T$ and compatible, up to the coherent homotopies of composition, with postcomposition of cocones by morphisms $T\to T'$.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 4.3.6.4 (018J), right anodyne/monomorphism case, for the pushout-join assertion; Example 4.3.6.5 (0235) for K empty and L the point. For the mapping-space assertion, Proposition 7.2.1.3 (02N3) identifies right anodyne monomorphisms with right cofinal monomorphisms, and the opposite-category dual of Proposition 7.2.2.1 (02NR), conditions (1) and (6), identifies right cofinality with restriction equivalences on coherent cocones. Naturality is that of the displayed precomposition functor. Read online, not archived in literature/. Tags here are Kerodon tags, not the unrelated Stacks tags with the same characters. Mapping-space convention check: Kerodon Construction 4.6.5.1 (01KX), Proposition 4.6.5.5 (01L0), and Proposition 4.6.5.10 (01L5). The natural pinch-inclusion equivalences identify the right-pinched model used here with the unadorned Hom spaces used in the cited cofinality/finality statements; after taking opposites use the left-pinch comparison as well.

proof.text: First compute the generating case $i:\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$, $0<i\leq n$, and $k:\partial\Delta^q\hookrightarrow\Delta^q$, $q\geq0$. A monotone map into the ordinal concatenation $[n]\star[q]=[n+q+1]$ splits uniquely into the initial block and the final block, giving $\Delta^n\star\Delta^q=\Delta^{n+q+1}$ by the join formula in the statement. By the horn definition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the first part $\Lambda_i^n\star\Delta^q$ is the union of the codimension-one faces omitting a vertex $j\leq n$, $j\ne i$. The second part $\Delta^n\star\partial\Delta^q$ adds exactly the codimension-one faces omitting a vertex $j>n$. Their intersection is $\Lambda_i^n\star\partial\Delta^q$, so the pushout is their union: the horn $\Lambda_i^{n+q+1}$. Since $0<i\leq n<n+q+1$, this is an inner horn. This includes $q=0$, when the second part is $\Delta^n$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, final generating calculation; the ordinal identification of Lemma 4.3.6.16 is written out here.

proof.text: For a fixed boundary inclusion $k:\partial\Delta^q\hookrightarrow\Delta^q$, [lem-coef-infinity-pushout-join-saturation] says that the class of monomorphisms $i$ with inner-anodyne $\theta_{i,k}$ is weakly saturated. Step 1 puts all generating right horns in this class; the definition of right anodyne in the item therefore puts every right-anodyne $i$ in it. Now fix such an $i$. The same saturation lemma says that the class of $k$ with inner-anodyne $\theta_{i,k}$ is weakly saturated, and the preceding argument puts every boundary inclusion in it. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to any monomorphism $K\hookrightarrow L$. Its skeletal presentation attaches coproducts of boundary inclusions and then takes the countable composite. A coproduct of boundary inclusions lies in the class as well: well-order its set of summands, start with the coproduct of their domains, and successively replace each domain by its codomain; each successor map is a pushout of one boundary inclusion and the limit is the coproduct of the codomains. Pushout and transfinite-composition closure now put every skeletal successor map and its composite $K\hookrightarrow L$ in the class. This proves the pushout-join assertion for the given $i$ and every monomorphism $k$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, the two saturation reductions; Proposition 1.5.5.14 (0077), relative skeletal presentation.

proof.text: For the cocone clause, fix $p:B\to\mathcal C$ and $T\in\mathcal C$. Let $q_T:E_T\to\mathcal C$ be the fixed-target arrow projection of [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-target-right-fibration], which is a right fibration. For $H=B,A$ put $p_B=p$, $p_A=p\circ i$, and let $S_H$ be the fiber over $p_H$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(H,E_T)\to\operatorname{Fun}(H,\mathcal C)$. These fibers use the constant simplices at $p_H$; their $n$-simplices are maps $H\times\Delta^n\to E_T$ over $p_H\circ\mathrm{pr}_H$, by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation] with $E=E_T$, $S=\mathcal C$, and the given right-anodyne $i$. Pull its displayed map back along $S_A\to\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal C)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(A,\mathcal C)}\operatorname{Fun}(A,E_T)$, sending a section $s$ to $(p,s)$. Its pullback is precisely restriction $r:S_B\to S_A$. Thus $r$ is a trivial Kan fibration: each lifting square for a boundary inclusion maps to one for the exponential map; its filler together with the prescribed base simplex is a filler in the pullback. This is the boundary-lifting definition in [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], including dimension zero.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.4 and Proposition 4.6.4.13 (01KQ); the section-space pullback used in the proof of Proposition 7.2.1.3 (02N3).

proof.text: For $H=A,B$, put $D_H=\operatorname{Fun}(H,\mathcal C)$; this is a quasicategory by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], with no assumption on $H$ beyond smallness. Unwind $E_T$, curry the maps in Step 3, and use the canonical permutation of product factors: an $n$-simplex of $S_H$ is precisely a map $H\times\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal C$ restricting at $0$ to $p_H\circ\mathrm{pr}_H$ and at $1$ to the constant $T$. Hence $S_H$ is exactly the arrow mapping space $U_{D_H}(p_H,\Delta_HT)$ defined in [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. That lemma supplies natural homotopy equivalences of Kan complexes $j_H:\operatorname{Map}_{D_H}(p_H,\Delta_HT)\to S_H$. Naturality for the restriction functor $D_B\to D_A$ gives the commuting square with upper map the item’s mapping-space restriction and lower map $r$.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.10 and the internal-functor identification of the unpinched arrow mapping spaces; compare the section-space argument of Proposition 7.2.2.1, (6) and (7).

proof.text: The trivial Kan fibration $r:S_B\to S_A$ is a homotopy equivalence, as can be checked without any colimit existence. By [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms], lifting against $\varnothing\hookrightarrow S_A$ gives a section $s:S_A\to S_B$. Lift against the degreewise injective inclusion $S_B\times\partial\Delta^1\hookrightarrow S_B\times\Delta^1$, with endpoint maps $s\circ r$ and $\mathrm{id}_{S_B}$ and base map $r\circ\mathrm{pr}_{S_B}$. The lift is a simplicial homotopy between $s\circ r$ and the identity, while $r\circ s=\mathrm{id}_{S_A}$. Thus $r$ induces bijections on components and isomorphisms on all homotopy groups. In Step 4’s square, both vertical maps $j_H$ have the same property by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Commutativity therefore gives bijections on components and isomorphisms on homotopy groups for the upper restriction map as well: on each group its map is $(j_A)_*^{-1}r_*(j_B)_*$. This is the required equivalence of Kan complexes in the convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Proposition 7.2.1.3, first-direction argument; explicit section/homotopy proof of the trivial-fibration implication, with pinch comparison 01L5.

proof.text: Finally let $R:D_B\to D_A$ be restriction. The equality $R\circ\Delta_B=\Delta_A$ follows in every simplicial degree by precomposing with $i\times\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^n}$. Consequently the restriction maps in the statement vary with $T$ through the constant-diagram functors, rather than through any chosen inverse of an equivalence. For an edge $T\to T'$ and any coherent simplex witnessing postcomposition of a cocone $p\to\Delta_BT$, precomposing that simplex with $i$ gives the corresponding witness in $D_A$. The same equality holds for every higher simplex, so all the composition homotopies and their compatibilities restrict too. By the meanings of coherent transformations and higher simplices in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], this is precisely naturality in $T$ and compatibility with coherent postcomposition.

source.place: Naturality of the precomposition construction; written out from the internal functor and constant-diagram definitions.
